brief: Create a warm, relatable 25–35 second short-form comedy about a remote worker trying to look composed during a video call while their pet repeatedly causes small, harmless interruptions. Make the character sympathetic, the setup believable, the escalation visual, and the ending a kind unexpected payoff. Write a voiceover-friendly timed script with clear scene beats, without relying on on-screen text to explain the joke.
title: The Professional Facade
hook: A remote worker desperately trying to maintain a "corporate" persona while their cat treats the meeting like a playground.
script:
(0:00-0:05) [Medium shot] ALEX (30s) is wearing a crisp blazer and glasses, nodding seriously. 
VO: "Yes, I completely agree. The Q3 projections are looking very promising."

(0:05-0:12) [Tight shot] A cat’s paw slowly reaches from off-screen and begins batting at Alex’s ear. Alex doesn't move a muscle, but their eye twitches.
VO: "I think the key here is stability and focus."

(0:12-0:20) [Wide shot] The cat jumps onto the desk, walking directly across the keyboard. We hear "asdfghjkl" typed into the chat. Alex gently pushes the cat away with one hand while keeping a frozen, professional smile for the camera.
VO: "Exactly. We need a seamless transition."

(0:20-0:27) [Medium shot] The cat leaps onto Alex's shoulders, curling up and purring loudly. Alex sighs, looks at the camera, and finally breaks character, smiling warmly.
VO: "Actually... I think my assistant has some notes on this."

(0:27-0:30) [Close up] The cat lets out a tiny, loud meow.
VO: "Meeting adjourned."
caption: My boss thinks I’m a powerhouse. My cat knows I’m just a heated blanket. 🐈💻 #RemoteWork #WFHLife #CorporateComedy
